chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: A man divorces his wife, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, and she has a daughter who is a slave. He buys her. Is it permissible for him to sleep with her? He said: No.
And regarding the man who has the slave girl and her daughter with him, so he sleeps with one of the two, and she dies, and the other remains. Is it correct for him to sleep with her? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man sleeping with a slave and her daughter simultaneously or consecutively in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the application of 'jam'' (gathering two sisters) specifically within the context of slave concubines, extending the Quranic prohibition to both free and enslaved women. It establishes that the prohibition is not limited to simultaneous possession but also applies to sequential possession if one sister dies while the other remains, ensuring the ruling's consistency across different marital and ownership scenarios.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man divorces his wife, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, and for her is a daughter, an owned slave. So he buys her. Is it Permissible for him that he sleeps with her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

And about the man who happened to have the owned slave girl with him, and her daughter. So he sleeps with one of the two, and she dies, and the other one remains. Is it correct for him that he sleeps with her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 13. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who divorces his wife and they become strangers to each other. She has a daughter who is a slave and he buys her; if he can go to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’

I asked him (the Imam) about the case of a man who has a slave-girl and her daughter and he goes to bed with one of them, then she dies and the other is living; if he can go to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’”
